display_name: Watches people and objects across the room
clinical_note: Distance vision matures in the 4-7 month window — baby now notices and tracks a person or pet moving across the room, not just things within arm's reach.

display_name: Rocks on tummy, kicks legs, and makes swimming motions
clinical_note: The 'airplane' posture — chest lifted, arms and legs pumping. Strengthens the back and hip muscles used for rolling.

display_name: Grabs her own feet and toes while lying on her back
clinical_note: Body-exploration play that builds core strength and hip flexibility. Feet often go straight to the mouth — that's expected.

display_name: Turns and twists a toy to look at all sides
clinical_note: Wrist rotation plus visual inspection — a step past simply holding or mouthing. Often paired with passing the toy between hands.

display_name: Bounces up and down when held in a standing position
clinical_note: Deliberate rhythmic leg-pushing while supported under the arms. Builds the leg strength used later for pulling to stand.

display_name: Gets up on hands and knees and rocks back and forth
clinical_note: Assuming the hands-and-knees position and rocking is the rehearsal stage before forward movement. Some babies skip it and scoot instead — also normal.

display_name: Catches himself with his arms when tipping over while sitting
clinical_note: Protective arm extension — reaching out to break a sideways or forward topple. Makes independent sitting safe enough for hands-busy play.

display_name: Shows new fears (vacuum cleaner, dark, loud noises)
clinical_note: New fears at this age reflect growing memory and anticipation, not regression. Comfort without avoiding the trigger entirely — repeated calm exposure helps.

display_name: Tests your reactions to his behavior (drops food and watches your response)
clinical_note: Deliberately repeating an action to see what you do — during meals and play. Social experimentation, not defiance.

display_name: Feeds herself small pieces of food with her fingers
clinical_note: Self-feeding combines the pincer grasp with hand-to-mouth accuracy. Offer soft, pea-sized pieces; mess is part of the learning.

display_name: Squats to pick something up, then stands back up
clinical_note: Controlled squat-and-return shows balance well beyond first steps. Usually appears within weeks of confident walking.
